newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT-RAINS SLOW MONTANA HARVEST.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT-RAINS SLOW MONTANA HARVEST.

text.p: Heavy rains stalled hard red winter and dark northern spring wheat harvest in northern Montana on Friday and forecasts called for more rains, several grain dealers said.

"It rained hard yesterday (Thursday) afternoon and evening," a northern Montana dealer said. "It cleared up most of the day and now it's raining hard again. They just don't need the rain anymore. Winter wheat harvest was 50 or 60 percent done and they were starting to cut the spring."
In southern Montana, clearer skies allowed for more harvest progress but movement remained slow.
One dealer said farmers continued to inquire about storage but few were willing to sell.
"We're not seeing much in here now because we're about to overflow," one dealer said. "We're up to our ears in storage business but we can barely buy a bushel."
In North Dakota, a few farmers planned to cut spring wheat this weekend, weather permitting. The storms that hit Montana on Friday were expected to move into North Dakota.
